note: Source of truth for the three VSLs (remake of 2026-11-12, John: no voice over, explain through text, very clear, motion graphics). Each beat is one card: `text` is the line on screen and in the .srt, `accent` the one phrase in the accent colour, `screen` the proof under it. Every command on screen is an sh line of README.md (a command inside a README `&&` chain counts) or a command of brand/demo/manifest.json, every terminal output line is a verbatim line of a manifest output field, every number comes from README.md, the package or the manifest. `ms` is not written by hand: build.py fit sets it from reading time (READ_MS_PER_WORD a word + READ_MS_BASE, at least MIN_BEAT_MS) plus the card's `proof_ms` for its animation. {site_url} and {repo_url} are filled at render time.

videos.name: vsl-90s
videos.title: Your agent deleted the tests. Here is how you get them back.

beats.text: Your agent just ran fourteen steps.
beats.visual: Frame one on Leader paper: the line builds word by word out of a mask, big, in Bricolage Grotesque; the step ruler at the top draws fourteen ticks left to right, the Record playhead riding the newest tick.

beats.text: Then it deleted your tests and overwrote your config.
beats.visual: Same scene, the camera still pushing in: the headline swaps (old line masks up and out, the new one rises in). A Spool panel under it: row twelve in Leader, then rows thirteen and fourteen type in and take the Rewind.

beats.text: Can you get them back?
beats.visual: Rewind wipe: the playhead sweeps right to left across the frame and the old scene slides back under it. git status prints; the two deleted test paths are struck through in Rewind, one after the other.

beats.text: Three parts: the problem, how it works, the fix.
beats.visual: A roadmap: three ticks on a short rule, each label rising in under its tick as the line names it; the problem in Record, the parts still to come in Tape.

beats.text: Why can't git help? The third test was never committed.
screen: untracked: git has no copy of it
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. The ruler's playhead scrubs back from fourteen to six and two Rule brackets close round tick six. The step six row (the agent wrote tests/test_timeout.py) prints in Rewind; a never committed tag in Tape under it.
cites: tracked and untracked files, but not git-ignored ones

beats.text: Claude Code's docs: shell-only changes aren't tracked.
screen: "A file that only Bash commands changed isn't tracked ..."
beats.visual: Rewind wipe to a quote card: the sentence from Claude Code's checkpointing page in Commit Mono builds in, isn't tracked underlined in Record; the source in Tape.
cites: A file that only Bash commands changed isn't tracked and stays as it is.

beats.text: So what would help? Think of a flight recorder.
beats.visual: Rewind wipe to a type card: the question, then the analogy, centred on paper, flight recorder in Record.

beats.text: It keeps every move, so you can replay it.
beats.visual: The analogy map draws: a hairline grid of two columns; flight recorder on the left, every move, kept on the right.

beats.text: So how does rewindagents record your agent?
screen: the agent's log   every tool call, kept
beats.visual: Same map, held: the second row lands under the first, aligned column for column, the agent's log in Record.
cites: Every tool call goes into a tamper-evident, hash-chained log

beats.text: Every tool call goes into one hash-chained log.
screen: each record holds the SHA-256 of the one before
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. Seven record cards in Spool draw in left to right, each joined to the one before by a hairline that draws as the card lands (the chain); the log path and the SHA-256 rule under them.
cites: Each record holds the SHA-256 of the record before it

beats.text: Before each edit or shell command, files are saved.
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. Two Rule brackets close round tick thirteen on the ruler; the step thirteen row in a Spool panel; on the beat only its three checkpointed mark turns Rewind; the note saved before, scanned after in Tape.
cites: the current bytes of the target file are copied
project's files before the command, scans again after it

beats.text: So which step would you rewind to?
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. rewindagents replay types; the last five rows print in Leader with nothing highlighted, the ruler full at fourteen. The frame holds: no answer shows before the next card.
cites: one line per step: number, tool, file or command

pause.answer: Step twelve, the last step before the delete.

beats.text: Twelve, because thirteen is the delete.
beats.visual: Same panel: row twelve takes the Rewind and the ruler's playhead scrubs back two ticks to twelve.

beats.text: One command, and four files come back.
screen: session demo: rewind to step 12 of 14 (did change 4 files)
beats.visual: Rewind wipe (the rewind itself). rewindagents rewind 12 types; the report prints with the four paths struck through, then the strikes pull back right to left one by one and the paths turn Rewind: the deleted files restoring in reverse.
cites: files back to how they were right after step 12
session demo: rewind to step 12 of 14 (did change 4 files)

beats.text: Even the rewind can be undone.
screen: session demo: rewind to step 12 of 14 (did change 4 files)
this rewind is step 15; undo it with: rewindagents rewind 14 --session demo
beats.visual: Same panel: the restore lines settle to Leader, the undo line prints in Rewind and a fifteenth tick grows on the ruler.
cites: this rewind is step 15; undo it with: rewindagents rewind 14 --session demo

beats.text: Where does the analogy break? Recorders can't undo a crash.
screen: the agent's log   every tool call, kept
flight recorder   can't undo the crash
beats.visual: Rewind wipe back to the analogy map: the two rows return in Tape and a third row draws under them, flight recorder, can't undo the crash.

beats.text: Unlike a recorder, this one puts your files back.
screen: the agent's log   every tool call, kept
flight recorder   can't undo the crash
the agent's log   rewind 12: files back
beats.visual: Same map: the fourth row, the agent's log, rewind 12: files back, lands in Record; the one row that has no flight-recorder twin.
cites: files back to how they were right after step 12

beats.text: Preview with diff. Take back one file with --only.
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. Two commands from the README, each typing into its own Spool chip as its sentence lands.
cites: what taking it back to step 12 would change
`rewind N --only PATH` puts back only those files

beats.text: You can now see every step and undo any of it.
beats.visual: Match cut: the ruler's playhead drops into the real rewindagents ui timeline (screenshot of the demo session), the camera pushes in on the rewound steps; the command in a small Spool chip, the 127.0.0.1 note in Tape.
cites: opens the timeline in your browser

beats.text: Up next: rewindagents init finds the seven agents it supports.
screen: Claude Code: has run in real sessions
Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Droid, Qwen Code:
tested with documented payloads, not yet in a live session
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. rewindagents init types in a Spool panel only as wide as the command; under it two bullet notes: Claude Code has run in real sessions (Reel), then the other six by name with their status on the line under, tested with documented payloads, not yet in a live session (both lines in Record).
cites: looks for the agents it supports (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Droid, Qwen Code)
The Claude Code hook has run in real sessions
tested with the documented payloads, not yet in a live session of any of them

beats.text: Apache-2.0. Standard library only. Not on PyPI yet.
screen: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only
beats.visual: Rewind wipe. The three short sentences build one a line; under them two ruled rows in Commit Mono rise in (the Python requirement, then the repository address, the one Record line), so the card never repeats its own words.
cites: No dependencies beyond the standard library

beats.text: Your editor has had undo for decades. Now your agent does.
screen: Ctrl+Z for AI coding agents: record, replay, rewind.
beats.visual: The last rewind wipe turns the paper to Reel: the line builds at the top in Leader, then the wordmark with its playhead in Rewind, the promise in Playhead, the address in Commit Mono and the credit line.
cites: Ctrl+Z for AI coding agents: record, replay and rewind.
